The first public release of Manifold Engine: a memory scanner, debugger and Lua scripting tool for Windows games, in the spirit of Cheat Engine.

## Highlights

- **Cheat Engine tables and scripts**: opens and saves `.CT` tables and runs their Auto Assembler and Lua scripts. Templates and most keyboard shortcuts carry over.
- **Scanner**: all the usual value types, an *All* scan over every number type at once, grouped scans, and results in RAM up to a limit, with the rest on disk.
- **Memory viewer and debugger**: a disassembler with symbols and jump arrows, a flow graph, write history with undo, conditional breakpoints that run inside the target, tracing, and "find out what accesses / writes". It works on 64-bit and 32-bit games, through the Windows debugger or in-process.
- **Game engines built in**: Unity (Mono and IL2CPP) with a scene explorer, .NET Framework and .NET games, Unreal Engine 4 and 5 without an SDK, and C++ RTTI. Structure Dissect shows the real class and field names.
- **More tools**: pointer scan with rescan, Code Filter, Signature Maker, speedhack, and struct export to C/C++, C# and ReClass.NET.
- **Scripting**: Lua 5.4 with the Cheat Engine API, plus the program's own checked `manifold` API, script windows in the program's look and a Form Editor.

## Getting started

1. Download `Manifold-Engine-1.0.0-win-x64.zip` below and unpack it into a folder you can write to, not `Program Files`.
2. Start `Manifold-Engine.exe`, open a game with `Ctrl+P` and a table with `Ctrl+O`.

You need 64-bit Windows and a graphics card with Direct3D 11. Many games need the program to run as administrator (Help → Restart as Administrator).

The `-symbols.zip` only holds debug symbols for reading crash reports. You do not need it to use the program.

## Please note

- Use it only on games you own or are allowed to study, and keep a backup of your saves. Memory edits can crash a game, and online use can get an account banned. Protected processes and anti-cheat systems are not supported.
- The program is not code-signed. Windows SmartScreen or an antivirus may warn about it, as they often do with memory tools.
- The Lua API starts at version 1 with this release (`manifold.apiVersion`). Autorun modules that ask for a higher API number will be held back.

Documentation: [README](https://github.com/Leunsel/Manifold-Engine#readme) and the [Docs folder](https://github.com/Leunsel/Manifold-Engine/tree/main/Docs). Bugs and ideas: [Issues](https://github.com/Leunsel/Manifold-Engine/issues).
